newsitem.title: USA: Argentina expects 30-35 airports to be privatized.
newsitem.headline: Argentina expects 30-35 airports to be privatized.

text.p: Argentina plans to grant a single concession to privatize at least 30 airports -- and possibly as many as 35 -- by late October, a senior Argentine airports official said Monday.

"Right now there are 30 airports to be concessioned, but we expect that to be expanded," Alfonso Ensinck, coordinator of Argentine airport systems, said speaking through a translator at a presentation for investors.

The country seeks bids for a single, 30-year concession to operate the airports, a process requiring about $2.0 billion of investment over the life of the deal, as well as payment of royalties to the Argentine government.
President Carlos Menem decreed the privatization in April after sell-off legislation stalled in Congress.
Argentina expects bids in early September and plans to award the concession on October 15, with final approval by Menem slated for November 5, Ensinck said.
"Flexibility will in no event be more than three weeks," he said.
Asked about potential roadblocks to the concession efforts, Ensinck said opponents' challenges pose little threat to the privatization.
"The government has always had the right to grant concessions in airports," he said.
He added that certain interests of Argentine businesman Alfredo Yabran "needed to be clarified," but he did not elaborate.
Yabran, who has acknowledged he has assets of $400 million, has denied opposition statements that he has any holdings in airport services.

In his New York presentation, Ensinck said the winning bidder will run concessions in car parking, restaurants and bars, ground transportation, car rental, fuel, banking and foreign exchange, advertising and tax-free operations.
Existing contracts of various maturities for duty-free retail, bonded warehousing, ground handling and catering, however, will be honored, he added..
